  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "f1",
      "concept_id": "c1",
      "text": "sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers automatic checkpointing after a transaction commits when the WAL contains N or more frames.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook() that causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f2",
      "concept_id": "c1",
      "text": "Passing N equal to zero or a negative value to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f3",
      "concept_id": "c1",
      "text": "Every new database connection enables automatic checkpointing by default at a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f4",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "A checkpoint must stop when it reaches a WAL page past the end mark of any current reader.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f5",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "Continuously overlapping readers can prevent every checkpoint from completing, causing the WAL file to grow without bound.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f6",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "Attempting checkpoints during reader gaps avoids the starvation scenario caused by continuously overlapping readers.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f7",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "If another process is checkpointing, checkpoint-lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f8",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "If the busy handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f9",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "A checkpoint that falls back to PASSIVE-style work after the busy handler stops waiting returns SQLITE_BUSY.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f10",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "Checkpointing requires syncing the WAL to persistent storage before copying its content into the database.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f11",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f12",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "Writers sync the WAL at every transaction commit with PRAGMA synchronous=FULL but omit that commit sync with PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "(Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync if PRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.)",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f13",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "Omitting disk synchronization sacrifices durability following a power loss or hard reboot.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Further, syncing the content to the disk is not required, as long as the application is willing to sacrifice durability following a power loss or hard reboot.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f14",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits until there is no writer and all readers use the most recent snapshot before checkpointing all frames and syncing the database file.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f15",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "While SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL is pending, it blocks new writers but permits new readers to continue.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f16",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART waits until all readers use only the database file, ensuring that the next writer restarts the log from the beginning.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f17",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "A writer rewinds the WAL when its entire content has been transferred into the database and synced and no readers are using the WAL.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f18",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "Normal checkpointing enables WAL reuse from the beginning without normally truncating the file, with journal_size_limit identified as an exception.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f19",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "COMMIT operations that trigger a checkpoint can be much slower than ordinary COMMIT operations.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "This has the effect of causing most COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger a checkpoint) to be much slower.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f20",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f21",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "A reader's end mark remains fixed throughout its transaction, preserving a database view from a single point in time.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "But for any particular reader, the end mark is unchanged for the duration of the transaction, thus ensuring that a single read transaction only sees the database content as it existed at a single point in time.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f22",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "The shared-memory wal-index requires readers on the same machine, preventing this SQLite WAL implementation from working on a network filesystem.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers, but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not work on a network filesystem.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f23",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers to finish.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish,",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f24",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f25",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "Automatic checkpoints and checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() use PASSIVE mode.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f26",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "Registering a callback with sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint().",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f27",
      "concept_id": "c13",
      "text": "The WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f28",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "SQLite WAL permits only one writer at a time because there is only one WAL file.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f29",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "For a checkpoint that can run, a non-NULL pnLog receives the total number of frames in the WAL.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f30",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "For a checkpoint that can run, a non-NULL pnCkpt includes frames checkpointed before the current function call.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If pnCkpt is not NULL,then *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f31",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "When zDb names an attached database outside WAL mode, the API returns SQLITE_OK with both checkpoint counters set to -1.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f32",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the log to zero bytes immediately before a successful return to the behavior of SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f33",
      "concept_id": "c17",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP exposes pnLog and pnCkpt without checkpointing any frames.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f34",
      "concept_id": "c18",
      "text": "After a crash or ROLLBACK, rollback-journal contents restore the database file to its original state.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "In the event of a crash or ROLLBACK , the original content contained in the rollback journal is played back into the database file to revert the database file to its original state.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f35",
      "concept_id": "c19",
      "text": "A NULL or empty zDb causes the requested checkpoint operation to be attempted on every WAL database attached to the connection.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f36",
      "concept_id": "c20",
      "text": "If WAL conversion fails because the VFS lacks the required shared-memory primitives, the existing journaling mode remains unchanged.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "If the conversion to WAL could not be completed (for example, if the VFS does not support the necessary shared-memory primitives) then the journaling mode will be unchanged",
      "pass": 0
    }
  ],

      "new_information_rate": 1.0
    }
  ],

claims.text: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers automatic checkpointing after a transaction commits when the WAL contains N or more frames.
claims.quote: The sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook() that causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.

claims.text: Passing N equal to zero or a negative value to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.
claims.quote: Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.

claims.text: Every new database connection enables automatic checkpointing by default at a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.
claims.quote: Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.

claims.text: A checkpoint must stop when it reaches a WAL page past the end mark of any current reader.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: Continuously overlapping readers can prevent every checkpoint from completing, causing the WAL file to grow without bound.
claims.quote: However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Attempting checkpoints during reader gaps avoids the starvation scenario caused by continuously overlapping readers.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: If another process is checkpointing, checkpoint-lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.
claims.quote: If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: If the busy handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.
claims.quote: If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE

claims.text: A checkpoint that falls back to PASSIVE-style work after the busy handler stops waiting returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.

claims.text: Checkpointing requires syncing the WAL to persistent storage before copying its content into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.

claims.text: Writers sync the WAL at every transaction commit with PRAGMA synchronous=FULL but omit that commit sync with PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL.
claims.quote: (Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync if PRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.)

claims.text: Omitting disk synchronization sacrifices durability following a power loss or hard reboot.
claims.quote: Further, syncing the content to the disk is not required, as long as the application is willing to sacrifice durability following a power loss or hard reboot.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits until there is no writer and all readers use the most recent snapshot before checkpointing all frames and syncing the database file.
claims.quote: This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.

claims.text: While SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL is pending, it blocks new writers but permits new readers to continue.
claims.quote: This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART waits until all readers use only the database file, ensuring that the next writer restarts the log from the beginning.
claims.quote: until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.

claims.text: A writer rewinds the WAL when its entire content has been transferred into the database and synced and no readers are using the WAL.
claims.quote: if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning

claims.text: Normal checkpointing enables WAL reuse from the beginning without normally truncating the file, with journal_size_limit identified as an exception.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.

claims.text: COMMIT operations that trigger a checkpoint can be much slower than ordinary COMMIT operations.
claims.quote: This has the effect of causing most COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger a checkpoint) to be much slower.

claims.text: With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.
claims.quote: Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).

claims.text: A reader's end mark remains fixed throughout its transaction, preserving a database view from a single point in time.
claims.quote: But for any particular reader, the end mark is unchanged for the duration of the transaction, thus ensuring that a single read transaction only sees the database content as it existed at a single point in time.

claims.text: The shared-memory wal-index requires readers on the same machine, preventing this SQLite WAL implementation from working on a network filesystem.
claims.quote: The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers, but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not work on a network filesystem.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers to finish.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish,

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.
claims.quote: The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.

claims.text: Automatic checkpoints and checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() use PASSIVE mode.
claims.quote: All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.

claims.text: Registering a callback with sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint().
claims.quote: Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.

claims.text: The WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.

claims.text: SQLite WAL permits only one writer at a time because there is only one WAL file.
claims.quote: However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.

claims.text: For a checkpoint that can run, a non-NULL pnLog receives the total number of frames in the WAL.
claims.quote: If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file

claims.text: For a checkpoint that can run, a non-NULL pnCkpt includes frames checkpointed before the current function call.
claims.quote: If pnCkpt is not NULL,then *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)

claims.text: When zDb names an attached database outside WAL mode, the API returns SQLITE_OK with both checkpoint counters set to -1.
claims.quote: If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the log to zero bytes immediately before a successful return to the behavior of SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP exposes pnLog and pnCkpt without checkpointing any frames.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: After a crash or ROLLBACK, rollback-journal contents restore the database file to its original state.
claims.quote: In the event of a crash or ROLLBACK , the original content contained in the rollback journal is played back into the database file to revert the database file to its original state.

claims.text: A NULL or empty zDb causes the requested checkpoint operation to be attempted on every WAL database attached to the connection.
claims.quote: If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.

claims.text: If WAL conversion fails because the VFS lacks the required shared-memory primitives, the existing journaling mode remains unchanged.
claims.quote: If the conversion to WAL could not be completed (for example, if the VFS does not support the necessary shared-memory primitives) then the journaling mode will be unchanged
